Subject: Re: Redshifts shifted after upgrade to lumenfit 2.5.0?

I did read the changelog, before upgrading and again after your reply. The cause is PR #812, merged Oct 22. In LineList.__init__, the default changed from wave_frame='air' to wave_frame='vacuum'. My spectra are wavelength-calibrated in air, so rest wavelengths are now vacuum by default. The vacuum/air ratio at H-alpha is about 1.00028, which is an 83 km/s offset, exactly what I measured, in the same direction for every object. This is a reproducible change in library behavior, not a calibration or config error on my side.

I spent two days thinking my wavelength calibration was broken and re-reduced arc lamps for 40 spectra for nothing, because nothing in the release notes suggested the default frame had changed. m_okonkwo also reports a small offset in this thread, so this is not just me. "Works for me" is not a test unless you confirm the frame of your own data; if it is vacuum or radio data, of course you would see no difference.

Marking the thread solved on the basis of a single "works for me" was premature and wasted my time. Please reopen it and mark it unsolved. The changelog entry for #812 says only "refactor", which does not tell anyone that a default changed. At minimum, CHANGES should explicitly say that LineList now defaults to wave_frame='vacuum'. Better, lumenfit should emit a warning when wave_frame is not explicitly set. A clear warning would have saved me two days and 40 unnecessary reductions.

Workaround for anyone else with air-calibrated spectra: LineList(..., wave_frame='air') restores the 2.4.3 behavior. I have written this up in the docs.
